title: Compute least actual-body borrowing on fixed Count tapes
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR3486 proves the least admitted borrowing at the actual body depth but leaves its encoded implementation and setup bill open. This adds an opt-in Count-tape selector for that exact covering contract: fixed `w`, strict `2k<e`, body `n=floor((e-k)/w)>=m`, and `q^k>=S_D(n)`.

All input-dependent arithmetic stays on tapes. Encoded bisection recomputes every trial's body/depth/stock and materializes a fresh final plan. The setup proof includes full rejected-trial radix powers, final recomputation and cleanup: `O(h^3+h^2(e+wh)^2)` tape operations and a conservative 24-role allowance, including the borrowed input, within the inherited 64-role setup inventory.

The reduced `e=13` case fits with `k=6` where the earlier `D(e)` selector requires 8 and fails. At `e=24`, substitution cycles `8→11→8`; the exact tape selector returns `k=9`. The threshold theorem remains PR3486's result.

Only `research/encoded-body-depth-borrowing/` changes. No default backend, selected payload, supplier, cutoff, κ or selected-frontier change is claimed. Completed-callee, pointwise restoration and physical/ordinary C0 premises remain conditional.

## Task and overlap

- Canonical base: `6f100d4bb5083f8c35d96fd95a539811c62f245c`, priority revision 6.
- `selected-stock-envelope`, scope **changed** to [PR3486's explicit handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-19010306), exact head `991861d40a1ebdbbf35be9adc1726e6af5b71e49`.
- [Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-19010614). Entry coverage: 410 open PRs and 2,332 Discussion records, complete pagination; focused publication refresh found unchanged main/predecessor.
- The concurrent [factor-two padding claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-19010608) permits `S/2<R<S` and explicitly excludes a full encoded borrowing selector. This package retains `R>=S`; no claim transfers across those predicates.

## Validation

At `232b3916e6331222278f6edd5a4b9d56731667d9`, Python 3.12 standard-library checks pass:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/encoded-body-depth-borrowing
python3.12 -I -O -B research/encoded-body-depth-borrowing/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/encoded-body-depth-borrowing --check-source-history
```

171 literal Count cases (84 fitted), 5,760 independent forward/slab cases, 12 rejection controls and an observed peak of 19 setup roles. Five actual implementation mutants reach the semantic oracle. Borrowed input, successful/fallback cleanup and an injected completed-trial failure are checked. A scan-origin bug caught by literal execution was corrected before publication and recorded in TASK.json.

Committed-byte/history checks, the 30-file export integrity check and optimized Git-free export replay pass. Runtime needs only unchanged main inputs; the pending predecessor proof is retained byte-for-byte without an external Git-object dependency. No selected GL64 payload, full selected cold replay or formal proof-kernel check was run. Arbitrary interruption/allocation-failure recovery inside inherited arithmetic is unclaimed.

## Credit

Hiroki Kumazaki, with substantial OpenAI Codex analysis, implementation, execution, writing and separate same-session AI-agent checks; no independent human review claimed. Apache-2.0. Credit Nick Petalas (#3486/#3246), Tekalign (#3264), Jose Manuel (#2899/#2809), David Arias (#2753), Ross Richardson (#2420), and their retained BIT/geometry/compiler lineage. Exact attribution and source pins are in the package.

## Open next questions

Bind this plan factory to one complete reduced ordinary caller, checking both padded returns, spectators and fallback. Separately, a saturated comparison could avoid full rejected-trial powers, but needs its own equivalence proof and final exact materialization. Both next steps are scoped in README.md; neither is claimed here.
